question.value: Does dust scattering reduce the observed mm continuum intensity in the inner (<~10 au) TW Hya disk, and what dust mass and grain size does this imply?

evidence.quote: We investigate whether the dust scattering indeed reduces the observed continuum intensity by comparing the ALMA archival data of the TW Hya disk

analysis_steps.goal: Radiative transfer models with and without scattering

method.value: RADMC-3D Monte Carlo with Mie opacities, power-law dust size distribution, Sigma_d ∝ r^-0.5, T ∝ r^-0.4; simulated images convolved with beam; vary T10, tau10, a_max

evidence.quote: radiative transfer simulations are performed with the Monte Carlo radiative transfer code RADMC-3D (cite: RADMC).

evidence.quote: The dust size distribution is assumed to be a power-law distribution ranging from 0.1 ${\rm \mu m}$ to $a_{\rm max}$ with the power-law index of 3.5.

assumptions.value: Compact spherical grains, density 1.675 g cm^-3; inclination 7 deg; DSHARP opacity

evidence.quote: The dust grains are assumed to be spherical compact grains with the material density of 1.675 ${\rm g~cm^{-3}}$.

fitting.value: Manual comparison of model grids to SED; tau10 set to match Band 3 intensity

evidence.quote: the disk mass (i.e., $\tau_{10}$) is set for each temperature model so that the observed intensity at Band 3 is reproduced

findings_qualitative.value: Model with scattering and 300 µm grains reproduces the SED dip at Band 7; no-scattering model is also consistent within flux errors, leaving a degeneracy.

evidence.loc: 4.6 Solving a degeneracy between models with and without scattering
evidence.quote: Although the model with scattering well reproduces the observed millimeter SED, the model without scattering is also consistent with the observations within the errors in the absolute intensities.

claims.hypothesis: Dust scattering reduces observed mm intensity in the inner TW Hya disk
claims.experiment: Multi-band SED at common beam compared with RADMC-3D models with and without scattering
claims.result: Scattering model with 300 µm grains fits; Band 7 intensity reduced ~35%
claims.finding: Scattering can hide large dust mass; Sigma_d ~10 g/cm2 at 10 au, 26x previous estimate

evidence.quote: We find that the model with scattering by 300 ${\rm \mu m}$-sized grains well reproduces the observed SED of the central part of the TW Hya disk

claims.hypothesis: Scattering is required to explain the SED
claims.result: Only T10=22 K, tau10=2.2 fits, within errors
claims.finding: Degeneracy remains; Band 10 could break it

evidence.loc: 4.6 Solving a degeneracy between models with and without scattering
evidence.quote: Due to the errors, it is not easy to solve the degeneracy between these models.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Carbonaceous (cosmic carbon) dust rejected because its flat albedo cannot make the Band 7 dip

evidence.quote: It indicates that the cosmic carbon dust might not account for the observed intensity profile of the inner region of the TW Hya disk which has a dip at Band 7.

limitations_admitted.value: Flux calibration uncertainties may be larger than official values; absolute opacity is uncertain.

evidence.quote: We confirmed that the actual uncertainty might be potentially larger than the official value but has little impact on our conclusion.

Results depend on DSHARP opacity and fixed temperature/density profiles
